extracted.intended_audience: TV industry readers, comedy fans, journalists and producers tracking pilots and series orders
extracted.subtask_description: A compiled industry guide that catalogs 2019 Comedy Central comedy pilots and straight-to-series orders, listing for each title its order status, episode count, production studio, creative team, logline, cast, and any source/origin notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page enumerates networks at the top (Comedy Central and many others) to indicate where a pilot/series order is placed or categorized. Example: this guide is titled '2019 Comedy Central Pilots & Series Orders' — network identifies the broadcaster/platform that ordered or will air the show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listings are grouped by year; the year indicates the season/upfront cycle or calendar year of the pilot/order. The page includes a year selector (2013–2026) and is focused on 2019 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre / Category
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre label for the listing (e.g., Comedy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listing is classified by genre; here entries appear under 'Comedy'. Genre signals tone and audience expectations for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order status (Picked up to series / Ordered straight to series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Status line describing how the show was commissioned (e.g., 'Picked up to series', 'Ordered straight to series').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This field indicates whether the project was picked up after a pilot or ordered straight to series. Examples: 'Picked up to series; 10 episodes' vs. 'Ordered straight to series; 20 episodes.' Status conveys network confidence and development path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode count
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of episodes ordered (e.g., '10 episodes', '20 episodes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often shown on the same line as status; episode count quantifies the initial series order and can signal whether it's a short first season, full season, or large straight-to-series commitment. Examples on the page: '10 episodes' for Awkwafina; '20 episodes' for Chasers and Crank Yankers.

rubrics_metrics.name: STUDIO
rubrics_metrics.description: Production studio / studio credit for the project (labelled 'STUDIO:').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the studio or producing company attached to the project, when provided. Example: 'Kimmelot' listed as STUDIO for Crank Yankers. Studio credit identifies which production entity handles show logistics, financing and packaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative team and production credits (labelled 'TEAM:'), often with parenthetical role abbreviations (w, ep, d, co-ep).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This field enumerates writers, executive producers, directors and other key creatives. The page uses abbreviations such as 'w' (writer), 'd' (director), 'ep' (executive producer), 'co-ep' (co-executive producer). Examples: 'Awkwafina (w, ep), Karey Dornetto (w, ep), Teresa Hsiao (w, co-ep), Lucia Aniello (d, ep)'. Use the TEAM block to assess pedigree, creative leadership and attached talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOGLINE
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise premise/summary of the show's concept (labelled 'LOGLINE:').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A one- or two-sentence description that communicates the premise, main character(s), setting and tone. Examples: 'Awkwafina is a twentysomething writer, actor and rapper living in Queens who strives for a larger-than-life existence while living with her father and grandmother.' Use the logline to quickly evaluate concept clarity and comedic hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAST
rubrics_metrics.description: Cast information (labelled 'CAST:'), including lead and recurring performers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the actors attached to the project, noting if roles are recurring. Examples: 'Awkwafina, BD Wong, Lori Tan Chinn, Chrissie Fit, Jennifer Esposito (recurring)'. Cast indicates star power, diversity, and potential audience draw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source / Origin notes (e.g., 'Based on', 'Revival')
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional provenance notes about the project such as 'Based on ___' or 'Revival of ___' included in listing copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides context on whether a project is an original concept, based on real life, adapted, or a revival. Examples on the page: 'Based on Roy Wood Jr.’s early life.' and 'Revival of 2002-07 series.' These notes affect expectations about audience familiarity and creative approach.
